items.title: Shell Launches Four Synthetic Lubricants For Indian Auto Aftermarket
items.summary: Shell Lubricants announced that it has introduced a four-product synthetic lubricant range for India's automotive aftermarket across its Shell Helix, Shell Advance, and Shell Rimula brands. The new lineup will target modern powertrains across passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, and commercial vehicles.

items.title: New Hyundai Bayon midsize SUV sells 3,449 units in first month
items.summary: Hyundai Motor India’s recently launched Bayon midsize SUV opened its domestic market sales account with factory dispatches (wholesales) of 3,449 units in October. In the process, the newest Hyundai SUV in town contributed 5% to the company’s highest-ever passenger vehicle wholesales of 62,799 units, up 17% YoY, and 8% to dispatches of 43,689 utility vehicles, up 16% YoY.

items.title: BS7 Tyre Emission Norms Pose Testing Challenge for Tyre Makers
items.summary: India's proposed Bharat Stage 7 (BS7) emission regulations, which for the first time will look beyond tailpipe emissions to regulate tyre wear, present a new challenge for the Indian tyre industry. Apart from developing tyres to meet the proposed abrasion limits, the industry will first need to establish the infrastructure and protocols to measure and validate tyre emissions.

items.title: Government May Launch Another Round of Rare Earth Magnet Manufacturing Scheme: Hanif Qureshi
items.summary: The government may launch another round of its rare earth magnet manufacturing scheme, Dr Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), Government of India, said at the CII Future of Mobility in India Conference 2026. Savings under the existing scheme could facilitate another round of the initiative.

items.title: Navratri Sales Dip 5% on High Base Effect
items.summary: Vehicle retail sales during this year’s Navratri window slipped about 5% from last year, when the festival began on the same day that revised GST rates took effect, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). Retailers sold 11,40,658 vehicles between 11 and 20 October 2026, against 12,01,480 in the 2025 window, a fall of 5.06%.
